sources.institution: Myanmar National Portal
sources.title: A Brief History of Myanmar
sources.usage: Body read: Historical paragraphs 126–129: Konbaung 1752–1885; independence 4 January 1948; AFPFL through 27 October 1958; caretaker 28 October 1958–3 April 1960; Union Government from 4 April 1960. Nationalist wartime nationwide-control assertions and contemporary regime propaganda excluded.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Burma: recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.usage: Body read: Recognition body: independent sovereign state 4 January 1948, distinct from the 1947 provisional government and foreign-relations arrangements.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1961–1963, XXIII, Document 49: Burma, 1962 retrospective
sources.usage: Body read: Body distinguishes Ne Win caretaker government in October 1958 with U Nu consent from the March 1962 coup; identifies U Nu as premier displaced in 1962. Not evidence of continuous U Nu premiership throughout 1948–1958.

sources.institution: Nationaal Archief
sources.title: Governor-General and Council of the Netherlands Indies: archive context
sources.usage: Body read: Constitutional-context body: 1854 government regulation effective 1 May 1855; Crown-appointed Governor-General and Council of Indies; Volksraad created 1918; 1925 Staatsregeling brought co-legislative powers, with Council advisory. Administrative reach and local consent powers are not generalized into sovereignty.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Indonesia: The Constitution
sources.usage: Body read: Body paragraphs 1–10: provisional constitution 18 August 1945; sovereignty transfer/federal constitution 27 December 1949; unitary cabinet constitution ratified August 1950; martial law 14 March 1957; dissolution of Constituent Assembly and return to 1945 constitution 5 July 1959. Later New Order institutions omitted.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Indonesia: recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.usage: Body read: Recognition body records Republic of United States of Indonesia recognition on 28 December 1949, not the date of Dutch sovereignty transfer.

sources.institution: Republic of Indonesia, State Secretariat
sources.title: Address on the 64th anniversary of the proclamation, 14 August 2009
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body distinguishes 17 August proclamation, next-day constitution and 5 July 1959 return to the 1945 constitution; presidential Guided Democracy through 1966. Broad shorthand for all 1945–1959 parliamentary institutions not adopted.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1958–1960, XVII, Document 224, 10 September 1959
sources.usage: Body read: Opening body explicitly dates first Guided Democracy cabinet under Sukarno premiership to 10 July 1959; Army expanding practical role and party exclusions. Later regime continuity corroborated by historical presidential address, not extrapolated from this single memo alone.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Thailand: The Chakkri Dynasty
sources.usage: Body read: Body: Rama I founded dynasty in 1782 and moved court to Bangkok; nineteenth-century royal diplomacy and monarchy. No automatic dynastic succession rule and suzerainty distinct from modern boundaries.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Thailand: 1932 Coup
sources.usage: Body read: Body: absolute monarchy ended 24 June 1932; provisional constitution three days later; permanent constitution before year end; National Assembly and cabinet with practical promoter/Army power; 1933 suspension/restoration and 1935 regency.

sources.institution: National Assembly of Thailand
sources.title: The National Assembly of Thailand: parliamentary guide
sources.usage: Body read: PDF historical pages 4–5: 24 June 1932 transition, temporary act 27 June, nominated first assembly 28 June. Formal constitutional change does not by itself establish unrestricted democracy.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Thailand: Sarit’s Return
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body: Sarit personal power October 1958, parties outlawed, critics jailed, prime minister and military dictatorship into early 1960s; monarchy used for legitimation. Erroneous January 1960 interim-constitution date not used.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1958–1960, XV, Document 534, 20 October 1959
sources.usage: Body read: Dated body corroborates authoritarian military government under Sarit; descriptive US policy preferences and claimed freedoms not adopted as objective regime quality.

sources.institution: Archives nationales d’outre-mer
sources.title: Indochine: research guide
sources.usage: Body read: Administration body: 1887 Union under Governor-General includes Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia; Laos added 1893; resident-superiors in four protectorates and Governor in directly administered Cochinchina; exclusively French before 1940. Formal organization through 1945 is not sole evidence of wartime practical sovereignty.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Cambodia: Domestic Developments
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body: Sihanouk abdicated 2 March 1955; father Suramarit king; Sangkum electoral domination September 1955. Sihanouk political leadership is distinguished from kingship and continuously held premiership.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Laos: The Kingdom of Laos
sources.usage: Body read: Body: constitution promulgated by Sisavang Vong 11 May 1947 declared independence within French Union; National Assembly invested government November 1947; 19 July 1949 convention enlarged foreign-affairs latitude with later power transfers. Formal declaration does not imply all French powers ended in 1947.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Dien Bien Phu and the Fall of French Indochina, 1954
sources.usage: Body read: Body identifies temporary 17th-parallel military demarcation and divided administrations after Geneva. Review only: no North/South choice for generic Vietnam from polygon location and no permanent legal-state partition inferred.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Vietnam: The Tay Son Rebellion
sources.usage: Body read: Body describes Tay Son and Nguyen Anh rivalry; Nguyen regained Gia Dinh in 1788 and Quy Nhon in 1799, Hue 1801 and Hanoi 1802. Generic Đại Việt in 1800 cannot silently become a unified later Nguyen state.

sources.institution: National Library Board Singapore, BiblioAsia
sources.title: British Malaya and Frank Swettenham
sources.usage: Body read: Article body distinguishes Straits possessions, indirectly ruled Federated Malay States and other Malay states outside British protection; historical use of Malaya as if a country. Review only, not automatic single-polity FMS assignment.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Malaysia: recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body: Federation of Malaya independent 31 August 1957; Malaysia formed in 1963 with Singapore, Sarawak and North Borneo. Raw Malaysia 1920–1960 is not projected into that later federation.

sources.institution: Permanent Mission of Brunei Darussalam to the United Nations
sources.title: Country Facts: History
sources.usage: Body read: Full body fetched and read in bruneiUN.html: British protectorate 1888, Resident system 1906 except religion/custom, 1959 written constitution and internal self-government, 1971 revision, independence only 1984. Modern ministerial portfolios not projected backward.

sources.institution: US House of Representatives, History Art and Archives
sources.title: The Philippines, 1898–1946
sources.usage: Body read: Body sections Civil Administration, Statutory Representation, Toward Independence and War: Governor-General/appointed Commission/elected Assembly after 1907; Jones Act 29 August 1916; 1934 authorization distinguished from 1935 presidency; US high commissioner and retained authority; wartime occupation/exile not generalized as prewar control.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Philippines: The Jones Act
sources.usage: Body read: Body: appointed Governor-General controls executive, Senate replaces Commission, mostly elected legislature with appointed minority; Jones law persists until new commonwealth legislation effective 1935.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Philippines: Commonwealth Politics, 1935–41
sources.usage: Body read: Body: 1935 commonwealth constitution, Quezon president, self-government but US foreign policy and approval of specified laws. Source shorthand Congress not used to claim original bicameral legislature.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Philippines: The Magsaysay, Garcia, and Macapagal Administrations
sources.usage: Body read: Body: Garcia accession March 1957 and election that year, Macapagal vice president of different party, Garcia presidency until 1961 election; 1959 base-jurisdiction negotiations distinguish independence from US military presence.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Philippines: recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.usage: Body read: Body: independent Republic recognized 4 July 1946 and US renounced sovereignty by treaty. Modern flag is not curated.

sources.institution: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand, edited by Dr Dhiravat na Pombejra
sources.title: Historical chronology: Ayutthaya to Bangkok (Rattanakosin)
sources.usage: Body read: PDF page 4 explicitly identifies accession of Rama I in 1782 as the beginning of Chakri Dynasty and Bangkok (Rattanakosin) era; establishes the historical name link, not later automatic government continuity.

sources.title: Meşrutiyet: constitutional reforms21August1909
sources.institution: TÜBİTAK, Cezmi Eraslan, Social Sciences Encyclopedia
sources.usage: Coordinator BODY read second-constitutional-era paragraph:21August1909 reforms, parliamentary accountability. Conflicting1878April assertion excluded; English TBMM8August1909 not normalized Gregorian.

sources.title: Meclis-i Mebusan: first constitutional era, institutional thesis record
sources.institution: Marmara University, Mesude Pınar Kaya,2000
sources.usage: Coordinator BODY read Turkish chronology paragraphs89–90 dates suspension13February1878; English abstract mistranslates18February and TBMM English says14February. Conflicting exact days are not forced:February1878 is a transparent coverage gap pending primary calendar verification.
